methodology: Rank repository-evidenced product need first, then React Aria compatibility, accessibility risk, explicit 1k/10k requirements, and implementation/migration/maintenance cost. Mandatory prototypes receive no automatic rank bonus.

demandEvidence.claim: The approved roadmap requires sorting and first-class server-side sorting.
The current public Table already documents controlled sorting.

records.reactAriaCompatibility: React Aria Table natively accepts sortDescriptor/onSortChange and Column allowsSorting.
accessibilityRisks: Sort direction must remain announced by React Aria.
Server refreshes must retain focus and stable column IDs.
records.stateModel: One SortDescriptor in the shared controller; every change increments the table query revision.
records.controlledUncontrolled: Support controlled sortDescriptor and defaultSortDescriptor without mirroring controlled state.
records.clientServer: Client mode uses a stable comparator; server mode publishes the same descriptor with cancellation and stale-result rejection.
records.ssrHydration: The initial descriptor and column IDs must be deterministic on server and client.

performance.rows1k: Measure stable local O(n log n) sorting; server mode remains available.
performance.rows10k: Prefer server sorting or deliberate memoized local sorting; capture both before promotion.

cost.implementation: Low: current Table and React Aria already expose the state contract.
cost.migration: Low: existing direct sort props remain supported.
cost.maintenance: Low: preserve React Aria descriptors and avoid a second sorting model.

records.rankingRationale: Existing public behavior plus an explicit server-side roadmap requirement makes sorting the strongest incremental plugin candidate.

demandEvidence.claim: The approved roadmap requires selection in the plugin research scope.
The current public Table documents React Aria selection modes.

records.reactAriaCompatibility: React Aria Table natively owns selectedKeys/onSelectionChange, selection modes, and keyboard semantics.
accessibilityRisks: Selection cannot be duplicated outside React Aria state.
Bulk selection and disabled rows require accurate announcements.
records.stateModel: One React Aria Selection value in the shared controller with stable row keys.
records.controlledUncontrolled: Support controlled selectedKeys and defaultSelectedKeys; controlled values remain authoritative.
records.clientServer: Selection is local identity state while server queries may consume the selected key snapshot.
records.ssrHydration: Default selection and row IDs must match across server render and hydration.

performance.rows1k: Measure Set cloning and membership without scanning every row.
performance.rows10k: Use key-based selection and the React Aria all-selection sentinel rather than materializing all keys.

cost.implementation: Low: React Aria already supplies selection behavior.
cost.migration: Low: direct selection props map to controller root props.
cost.maintenance: Low: retain React Aria Selection as the only representation.

records.rankingRationale: Selection already exists publicly and can validate shared-state composition without replacing accessible interaction behavior.

demandEvidence.claim: The roadmap explicitly requires first-class server-side pagination.
Tale UI already has an accessible standalone Pagination component available for composition.

records.reactAriaCompatibility: Pagination composes outside Table without replacing table semantics; the controller supplies page query state.
accessibilityRisks: Page changes must move or preserve focus intentionally.
Row counts and current page state require accessible labels.
records.stateModel: Page, page size, known/unknown total, and query revision belong to the shared controller.
records.controlledUncontrolled: Support controlled page/pageSize and deterministic defaults.
records.clientServer: Client mode slices a stable row set; server mode treats page changes as cancellable correlated requests.
records.ssrHydration: Initial page and page size must be identical during SSR and hydration.

performance.rows1k: Client slicing is bounded by page size and should not copy unrelated rows.
performance.rows10k: Server pagination is the default performance path when a backend is available.

cost.implementation: Medium: integrate query state with the existing Pagination component.
cost.migration: Low: standalone Pagination compositions can move handlers into the controller.
cost.maintenance: Medium: support unknown totals and server response correlation.

records.rankingRationale: The roadmap explicitly requires server pagination and Tale UI already owns the visual navigation primitive.

demandEvidence.claim: The roadmap explicitly requires first-class server-side filtering.

records.reactAriaCompatibility: Filtering is external query state and can change Table.Body rows without changing React Aria table semantics.
accessibilityRisks: Result changes need count/status announcements without excessive live-region noise.
Focus must be reconciled when the focused row is filtered out.
records.stateModel: A versioned filter expression joins sorting and pagination in the shared query snapshot.
records.controlledUncontrolled: Support controlled filters and deterministic default filters; schema design precedes public promotion.
records.clientServer: Client predicates and server expressions share revision/cancellation behavior but not executable serialization.
records.ssrHydration: Default filters and their resulting initial rows must be server/client deterministic.

performance.rows1k: Measure predicate cost and avoid recomputation for unrelated state.
performance.rows10k: Prefer server filtering or an explicitly benchmarked indexed client strategy.

cost.implementation: Medium: define a non-executable filter model and result announcements.
cost.migration: Medium: existing ad hoc predicates need explicit adapters.
cost.maintenance: Medium: client and server operators require compatibility discipline.

records.rankingRationale: Filtering is a named server-side acceptance requirement and must share request state with sorting and pagination.

demandEvidence.claim: The roadmap requires virtualization research and 1k/10k benchmarks.
Tale UI already exposes React Aria Virtualizer primitives.

records.reactAriaCompatibility: React Aria virtualization primitives exist, but Table integration and collection semantics require a dedicated prototype.
accessibilityRisks: Unmounted offscreen rows can change screen-reader browsing and row count expectations.
Focus restoration and virtualized measurement must survive zoom and dynamic content.
records.stateModel: Viewport and measurement state is plugin-local while row identity and query revision remain controller-owned.
records.controlledUncontrolled: Expose controlled layout inputs only where persistence is required; measurements remain internal.
records.clientServer: Virtualization composes with either client rows or server windows and must not imply pagination semantics.
records.ssrHydration: Use a deterministic non-virtualized or bounded initial window until client measurements are available.

performance.rows1k: Compare virtualized and non-virtualized rendering before choosing the crossover.
performance.rows10k: Require bounded mounted rows, scroll/focus evidence, and retained benchmark results.

cost.implementation: High: integrate layout, collection, focus, and measurement behavior.
cost.migration: Medium: consumers need a deterministic size/scroll contract.
cost.maintenance: High: browser, accessibility, and dynamic-row regressions require dedicated coverage.

records.rankingRationale: The explicit 10k-row gate makes a bounded rendering path more consequential than convenience-only column plugins.

demandEvidence.claim: The approved plan freezes column visibility/settings in the exact evaluation inventory.

records.reactAriaCompatibility: Visible columns can be derived before Table.Header/Table.Body render while retaining stable column keys.
accessibilityRisks: Hiding a focused or row-header column requires deliberate focus and announcement behavior.
At least one row-header column must remain available.
records.stateModel: A set of visible stable column IDs belongs to the shared controller.
records.controlledUncontrolled: Support controlled visibleColumnIds and a deterministic default set.
records.clientServer: Visibility is normally client state; servers may consume it only as an explicit projection hint.
records.ssrHydration: Persisted visibility cannot change the hydration tree before client state is reconciled.

performance.rows1k: Derive visible column definitions once per visibility revision.
performance.rows10k: Avoid per-cell visibility checks by projecting columns before row rendering.

cost.implementation: Medium: enforce row-header and focus invariants.
cost.migration: Medium: current conditional-column patterns need stable IDs.
cost.maintenance: Medium: persistence and responsive ownership must remain outside Table.

records.rankingRationale: Useful shared state, but it lacks the explicit server/performance pressure of the proposed top five.

demandEvidence.claim: Current Table documentation already acknowledges React Aria resizable column state.

records.reactAriaCompatibility: React Aria exposes resizable containers, column widths, and resize callbacks.
accessibilityRisks: Resize handles need keyboard operation and perceivable labels.
Minimum widths must preserve zoom and reflow usability.
records.stateModel: Column widths use stable column IDs and remain isolated from data query revisions.
records.controlledUncontrolled: Support controlled widths and defaults using React Aria column-size types.
records.clientServer: Resize is client presentation state and must not trigger data requests.
records.ssrHydration: Deterministic default widths render on the server; persisted widths apply after safe reconciliation.

performance.rows1k: Width changes should update column layout without rebuilding row data.
performance.rows10k: Throttle visual layout work through React Aria behavior and measure resize frames.

cost.implementation: Medium: add container/resizer wrappers and styling.
cost.maintenance: Medium: pointer, keyboard, RTL, and zoom behavior need coverage.

records.rankingRationale: Strong upstream compatibility lowers risk, but resize is presentation state rather than a core server-data workflow.

demandEvidence.claim: Current Table documentation exposes React Aria hierarchical expansion props.

records.reactAriaCompatibility: React Aria Table supports expandedKeys/defaultExpandedKeys and hierarchical rows.
accessibilityRisks: Expansion state and hierarchy levels must be announced.
Collapsed descendants must not retain unreachable focus.
records.stateModel: Expanded row keys use stable row IDs and may join server child-loading requests.
records.controlledUncontrolled: Preserve React Aria controlled/default expanded-key conventions.
records.clientServer: Client mode reveals existing children; server mode correlates child loading by row and query revision.
records.ssrHydration: Default expanded keys and available child rows must match across hydration.

performance.rows1k: Expansion should process affected branches rather than flattening every row.
performance.rows10k: Large expanded trees require windowing or server child loading.

cost.implementation: Medium: upstream behavior exists but shared async loading does not.
cost.migration: Low: current expansion props remain valid.
cost.maintenance: Medium: tree accessibility and lazy children require coverage.

records.rankingRationale: The base component already exposes expansion, so controller work is less urgent than missing query and performance capabilities.

demandEvidence.claim: The approved plan freezes sticky columns in the exact evaluation inventory.

records.reactAriaCompatibility: Sticky positioning can preserve native table semantics if DOM order and headers remain unchanged.
accessibilityRisks: Pinned content must not obscure focused cells at zoom.
RTL pinning and overlap order require explicit tests.
records.stateModel: Pinned leading/trailing column IDs are presentation state in the shared controller.
records.controlledUncontrolled: Support controlled pin sets and deterministic defaults only after the CSS contract is proven.
records.clientServer: Sticky state is client presentation state and never changes the data query.
records.ssrHydration: Default pinning must be deterministic; viewport-derived pinning waits until after hydration.

performance.rows1k: Measure paint and compositing cost with representative cell content.
performance.rows10k: Combine only with a proven bounded rendering strategy.

cost.implementation: Medium: coordinate offsets, resize, visibility, and RTL.
cost.maintenance: High: browser layout interactions with resize and virtualization.

records.rankingRationale: Sticky columns depend on unresolved visibility, resize, RTL, and virtualization contracts.

demandEvidence.claim: The approved plan freezes grouped/tree rows in the exact evaluation inventory.
The current Table exposes hierarchical rows but not a grouping controller.

records.reactAriaCompatibility: Hierarchical rows align with React Aria tree-grid behavior; data grouping and aggregation remain Tale-owned concerns.
accessibilityRisks: Group rows, levels, expansion, and aggregate labels need a complete tree-grid model.
Keyboard behavior must not conflict with row selection.
records.stateModel: Grouping descriptors, expanded keys, and stable derived group IDs share one controller.
records.controlledUncontrolled: Controlled grouping and expansion require deterministic derived IDs; defaults cannot depend on locale-sensitive labels.
records.clientServer: Client grouping derives branches; server grouping requires explicit aggregate and child contracts.
records.ssrHydration: Grouping, derived IDs, and expansion must produce identical trees on server and client.

performance.rows1k: Measure grouping and flattening independently from rendering.
performance.rows10k: Require server grouping or a benchmarked indexed tree plus virtualization.

cost.implementation: High: define grouping, aggregation, hierarchy, and selection interactions.
cost.migration: High: no current Tale grouping model exists.
cost.maintenance: High: complex accessibility, async, and performance matrix.

records.rankingRationale: This has the broadest unresolved data, accessibility, server, and migration contract, so it follows the foundational plugins.
